counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span describing a purely fatty encapsulated mass, which would favor lipoma
No raw span describing a cystic cavity or dermal appendages, which would favor dermoid cyst or teratoma
No raw span describing ectopic thyroid tissue or thyroid function testing, which would favor lingual thyroid
decisive_items: the lesion had been present since birth
the lesion appeared partly fatty, likely submucosal
response.rationale: R6 best integrates congenital onset, midline dorsal tongue location, soft smooth exophytic morphology, submucosal partly fatty imaging, and lack of muscle invasion. R4 is the closest runner-up but is discounted because the lesion is only partly fatty and shows mild enhancement, whereas a congenital lipoma would be predominantly fat. R5 lacks cystic/dermal raw evidence, R8 lacks fatty signal, and R7/R1 are discordant with the fatty, non-heterogeneous imaging pattern.

rejected.why: Congenital granular cell tumor is typically a non-fatty gingival epulis; the fatty MRI signal and dorsal tongue location are discordant.
Teratoma would require heterogeneous multi-germ-layer elements; the smooth, regular, soft, partly fatty lesion lacks such raw evidence.
Lingual thyroid would be a soft-tissue midline mass, not partly fatty; no raw evidence of thyroid tissue or function is supplied.
Dermoid cyst would be cystic and usually floor-of-mouth; no raw span for cyst wall, dermal elements, or cystic imaging is present.
